{{Short description|Chilean mathematical physicist}}

'''Patricio Anibal Letelier Sotomayor''' (September 11, 1943 – June 9, 2011) was a Chilean [[mathematical physicist]] and professor at [[State University of Campinas|University of Campinas]] (UNICAMP).

== Work ==
Letelier was born in [[Santiago]]. Early in his career (1993) Letelier worked with Dmitrii Vladimirovich Gal'tsov to define what has become known as the ''Letelier-Gal'tsov spacetime''.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |title=The Letelier-Gal'tsov spacetime revisited |language=en|eprint = gr-qc/0502014|last1=Clement|first1=G.|last2=Gal'tsov|first2=D. V.|last3=Letelier|first3=P. S.|year=2005}}</ref> He received his Ph.D. in Physics from the [[Boston University]] in 1977 under [[John Stachel]]. He joined the faculty of the [[University of Brasília]] until 1988 when became a Professor of Mathematical Physics in the Department of Applied Mathematics of UNICAMP.

He died on Thursday, June 9, 2011 of a cardiac arrest in his home in [[Campinas]].<ref name="uni-frankfurt">{{cite web|url=https://hyperspace.uni-frankfurt.de/2011/06/14/prof-letelier-passed-away/|title=Prof. Letelier passed away &#124; hyperspace@gu|website=hyperspace.uni-frankfurt.de|date=14 June 2011 |access-date=21 August 2019}}</ref>

In honor of  his work, an astronomer he advised for a doctor thesis, named an asteroid he had discovered after Letelier: (109879) Letelier.<ref name="asteroid">{{cite web|url=  https://www.minorplanetcenter.net/db_search/show_object?utf8=%E2%9C%93&object_id=109879|title=Asteroid Letelier|website=MinorPlanetCenter.net|access-date=January 9, 2023   }}</ref>
